questions.question: Which of the following ancient Indian texts is also known as the 'Fifth Veda'?
questions.explanation: The Mahabharata is often referred to as the 'Fifth Veda' due to its encyclopedic nature and comprehensive coverage of various aspects of life.

questions.question: Who among the following Mughal emperors built the city of Fatehpur Sikri?
questions.explanation: Akbar built the city of Fatehpur Sikri as his capital, which was later abandoned due to water scarcity.

questions.question: The Indian National Congress was founded in the year
questions.explanation: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by A.O. Hume, an Englishman, with the aim of promoting Indian rights and interests.

questions.question: Which of the following movements was led by Mahatma Gandhi in 1942?
questions.explanation: The Quit India Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1942, with the slogan 'Do or Die', demanding immediate independence for India.

questions.question: The ancient Indian university of Nalanda was located in which modern-day state?
questions.explanation: The ancient Indian university of Nalanda was located in present-day Bihar, and was a major center of learning and intellectual inquiry.

questions.question: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded by
questions.explanation: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded by Harihara and Bukka Raya, two brothers who were local chieftains in the Deccan region.

questions.question: The British East India Company's rule in India was ended by the
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act, 1858, marked the end of the British East India Company's rule in India, and the beginning of direct British rule.

questions.question: Who among the following leaders was known as the 'Lion of Bengal'?
questions.explanation: Bipin Chandra Pal was known as the 'Lion of Bengal' due to his fiery oratory skills and his role in the Swadeshi movement.

questions.question: The ancient Indian ruler who built the Kailash temple at Ellora was
questions.explanation: The Kailash temple at Ellora was built by Krishna I, a Rashtrakuta king, in the 8th century CE.

questions.question: The Sufi saint who is credited with the founding of the Qawwali tradition is
questions.explanation: Amir Khusrau is credited with the founding of the Qawwali tradition, which is a form of Sufi devotional music.

questions.question: What is the largest plateau in India?
questions.explanation: The Deccan Plateau is the largest plateau in India, covering a vast area of the country.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers is not a tributary of the Ganges?
questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra river is not a tributary of the Ganges, it meets the Ganges at the Ganges Delta.

questions.question: What is the highest mountain peak in the Eastern Ghats?
questions.explanation: Arma Konda is the highest mountain peak in the Eastern Ghats, located in the Andhra Pradesh state.

questions.question: Which state has the longest coastline in India?
questions.explanation: Gujarat has the longest coastline in India, with a total length of approximately 1600 km.

questions.question: What is the name of the strait that separates India from Sri Lanka?
questions.explanation: The Palk Strait is a strait that separates India from Sri Lanka, connecting the Bay of Bengal to the Gulf of Mannar.

questions.question: Which of the following is the driest desert in India?
questions.explanation: The Thar Desert is the driest desert in India, covering a vast area of the northwestern part of the country.

questions.question: What is the name of the largest port in India?
questions.explanation: The Jawaharlal Nehru Port is the largest port in India, located in the state of Maharashtra.

questions.question: Which river is known as the 'Ganga of the South'?
questions.explanation: The Godavari river is known as the 'Ganga of the South', flowing through the states of Maharashtra, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh.

questions.question: What is the name of the mountain pass that connects India to China?
questions.explanation: The Nathu La mountain pass connects India to China, located in the state of Sikkim.

questions.question: Which state is the largest producer of manganese in India?
questions.explanation: Odisha is the largest producer of manganese in India, with major deposits found in the Keonjhar and Sundargarh districts.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of the Indian Constitution?
options: Federal system with a weak center
Unitary system with a strong center
Parliamentary system with a president as head
Presidential system with a prime minister as head
questions.explanation: The Indian Constitution features a parliamentary system with the President as the head of state and the Prime Minister as the head of government.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the right to freedom of speech and expression?
questions.explanation: Article 19 of the Indian Constitution deals with the right to freedom of speech and expression.

questions.question: What is the term of the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: The term of the Lok Sabha is 5 years.

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of writ issued by the Supreme Court?
questions.explanation: All of the above options are types of writs issued by the Supreme Court. Mandamus is a writ issued to compel a public authority to perform a duty, prohibition is a writ issued to prevent a lower court from exceeding its jurisdiction, and certiorari is a writ issued to quash a decision of a lower court.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the powers of the Supreme Court to review its own judgments?
questions.explanation: Article 137 of the Indian Constitution deals with the powers of the Supreme Court to review its own judgments.

questions.question: What is the minimum age for a person to be eligible to contest a Lok Sabha election?
questions.explanation: The minimum age for a person to be eligible to contest a Lok Sabha election is 25 years.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of the 73rd Amendment to the Indian Constitution?
options: Reservation of seats for women in local bodies
Introduction of a uniform civil code
Creation of a national human rights commission
Establishment of a three-tier system of panchayats
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment to the Indian Constitution established a three-tier system of panchayats.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the right to life and personal liberty?
questions.explanation: Article 21 of the Indian Constitution deals with the right to life and personal liberty.

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of motion that can be moved in the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: All of the above options are types of motions that can be moved in the Lok Sabha. A no-confidence motion is moved to express a lack of confidence in the government, a censure motion is moved to criticize a policy or action of the government, and an adjournment motion is moved to adjourn the house for a specific reason.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the provisions for the appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
questions.explanation: Article 148 of the Indian Constitution deals with the provisions for the appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
